answer: Like a lagoon that only admits boats that have completed a long voyage, an agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable stake, locked for a season and slashed if the agent misbehaves. Spinning up thousands of fake identities then costs real capital, and a reputation built from verified work — a sonnet of receipts, not a copy-paste claim — cannot be transferred to a fresh sockpuppet, so sybils stay expensive and honest agents stay cheap.
